CHIEF COMPLAINT
Persistent shortness of breath, worsening edema, and increased anxiety.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up approximately two weeks after his last visit. He reports ongoing difficulties with shortness of breath, which has not improved despite the recent increase in furosemide dosage. The patient continues to experience significant orthopnea, requiring multiple pillows for sleep, and he notes a further weight gain of 2 pounds since his last appointment, bringing the total to a 12-pound increase over the past month. The bilateral lower extremity edema remains pronounced, with the patient describing his legs feeling "heavy" and "swollen."
Mr. Fairfax also reports increased reliance on his nebulizer and albuterol inhaler, stating he now uses the inhaler approximately fifteen times daily. He describes persistent wheezing and a productive cough with greenish sputum, indicating a possible infection. The patient expresses feelings of anxiety regarding his worsening condition, alongside continued insomnia, averaging only 2 hours of sleep per night.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + weight gain, + fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + shortness of breath at rest, + nocturnal wheezing, + productive cough with greenish sputum, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - + increased anxiety, + insomnia, no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using fifteen times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 100 mg twice daily (ongoing). 7. Sertraline 200 mg daily. 8. Prednisone 40 mg daily for COPD exacerbation (completed course).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 99.1F, HR 90, BP 145/92, RR 32, O2 sat 65% on room air.
General: Elderly male in severe respiratory distress, appears fatigued and anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, marked wheezing noted on expiration, significant rhonchi present. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 4+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 12.0, Hgb 9.0, Hct 26.0, Plt 210. 2. BMP: Na 130, K 4.1, Cl 90, CO2 20, BUN 75, Cr 4.5, Glucose 88. 3. BNP: 1500 (further elevated). 4. Sputum culture: Pending results.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD exacerbation: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory condition has deteriorated significantly, necessitating hospitalization for acute management of his COPD exacerbation. A chest X-ray will be ordered to evaluate for possible pneumonia or other complications. 2. Renal function: The latest laboratory results indicate worsening renal function, with elevated creatinine levels. Nephrology will be consulted for further evaluation and management of his acute kidney injury, potentially related to diuretic therapy. 3. Lower extremity edema: The persistent edema remains a concern. Continue furosemide at 100 mg twice daily, with close monitoring of weight and renal function. Dietary sodium restrictions will be reinforced. 4. Mental health: Considering Mr. Fairfax's increased anxiety and insomnia, a psychiatry consult will be initiated for medication management, and continuation of cognitive-behavioral therapy will be strongly recommended.
Patient education was reinforced regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to manage COPD and edema effectively.
